Generated on November 27, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea LECTURA_DECODIFIC_VOCABULARIO`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Vocabulario lector*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/LECTURA_DECODIFIC_VOCABULARIO.html). ::: **In one sentence.** Reading vocabulary, from age 7 to 10 (6,567 administrations in 4 cohorts; 2 forms). Revisar el número de ítems. *Age.term: provisional reading of the activity's label 3 (3rd digit = age, 4th = term; 0 = annual), to be confirmed with the engineer.* **How it looks on the platform** (first item or example; 2026 screenshot; the interface is in Spanish). ::: {layout-ncol=1} ![1950 · Cribado Vocabulario](../../figuras/plataforma/1950.jpg){.lightbox width="40%" fig-alt="Screenshot of activity 1950"} ::: ## Theoretical framework Vocabulary is knowledge of word meanings. The platform measures it in two ways: **orally**, when the child explains the meaning of a word they hear, and **through reading**, when they choose, among three written words, the one with a similar meaning. In the simple view of reading, vocabulary is part of language comprehension, the component that does not depend on reading [@hoover1990simple]. **What the evidence says:** - **Preschool oral language predicts reading comprehension years later.** Comprehension at age 8½ is explained by word reading at 5 and by language at 3½, in children at family risk of dyslexia and in the rest [@hulme2015foundations]. Language in the broad sense (vocabulary, grammar, inference) predicts it better than vocabulary alone [@lervag2018comprehension]. - **Written vocabulary is not only language.** Vocabulary tasks also capture variance from decoding, because the meaning, written form and phonology of each word are connected [@protopapas2013vocabulary]. - **The relation is reciprocal.** Reading more expands vocabulary, and a larger vocabulary makes it easier to read new words [@killingly2024reciprocal]. In the first school years the code (letters and phonological awareness) weighs more; later, word reading and comprehension separate [@storch2002oral]. **What our data show.** Vocabulary through reading predicts low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency almost as well as the reading tasks (median AUC .75), but it is not very stable between terms (ρ = .43). Oral vocabulary at ages 4 and 5 has good internal consistency (α = .82) and predicts less (median AUC .63, maximum .71). This is to be expected: its main role is in comprehension, not fluency. It is also one of the best predictors of arithmetic at ages 10–11 ([Numerical cognition](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/cognicion-numerica.html#sec-mate-criterio), *in Spanish*). ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point|Form | Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|:----|------:|-------:|:-----------|-----:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 7.2|1950 | 2012| 904|2019/20 | 221| 217| 0| 11| | 7.2|VOC | 2013| 2021|2020/21 | 1,294| 249| 115| 52| | 8.2|1950 | 2011| 905|2019/20 | 468| 0| 468| 23| | 8.2|VOC | 2012| 2021|2020/21 | 1,488| 152| 0| 51| | 9.2|VOC | 2011| 2021|2020/21 | 1,537| 0| 485| 52| | 10.2|VOC | 2010| 2021|2020/21 | 1,559| 111| 278| 52| |Form | Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness|% floor |% ceiling | |:----|----------:|---:|-------:|-----:|----:|------:|--------:|:-------|:---------| |1950 | 7.2| 217| 2012| 12.12| 6.28| 11.33| -0.14|NA |NA | |VOC | 7.2| 249| 2013| 10.56| 6.26| 9.67| 0.78|NA |NA | |VOC | 8.2| 152| 2012| 18.12| 7.41| 18.00| -0.01|NA |NA | |VOC | 10.2| 111| 2010| 26.34| 6.83| 27.33| -0.36|NA |NA | **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct − errors/3). Internal consistency from item-level responses is missing. As a timed task, stability is the preferred reliability estimate. | Cohort| From| To| n| r| ρ| |------:|----:|---:|---:|----:|----:| | 2011| 8.2| 9.2| 414| 0.27| 0.22| | 2012| 7.2| 8.2| 112| 0.65| 0.63| ## Validity **Concurrent.** Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Word and text reading (7.2, r = .64); Word and text reading (8.2, r = .56); Word and text reading (9.2, r = .57); Word and text reading (10.2, r = .56). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .66–.84. Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .51–.66. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_LECTURA_DECODIFIC_VOCABULARIO_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .72–.80 (4 time points; 299–411 children). ## Provisional norms |Form | Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |:----|----------:|-----:|-------:|----:|----:|----:|----:|----:|----:|----:| |1950 | 7.2| 217| 2012| 1.0| 5.0| 6.3| 8.0| 11.3| 15.3| 20.5| |VOC | 7.2| 249| 2013| 1.5| 3.3| 4.3| 6.3| 9.7| 14.0| 18.7| |1950 | 8.2| 468| 2011| 0.3| 1.7| 1.7| 1.7| 1.7| 1.7| 1.7| |VOC | 8.2| 152| 2012| 5.5| 7.7| 10.8| 13.6| 18.0| 23.3| 27.9| |VOC | 9.2| 1,537| 2011| 10.0| 12.5| 15.0| 17.3| 23.3| 28.3| 32.1| |VOC | 10.2| 111| 2010| 14.7| 16.7| 18.3| 21.5| 27.3| 31.3| 34.0| Each form (platform code) has its own norms, because the forms need not measure on the same scale. These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_LECTURA_DECODIFIC_VOCABULARIO_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ### Forms: can they be pooled? Forms given at the same time point are compared. They are considered **equivalent** if the mean difference is smaller than 0.20 SD and the SD ratio is between 0.80 and 1.25. If the same children took them, **linear equating** is also computed, which puts the second form on the scale of the first, together with the correlation between forms (parallel-forms reliability). The child reads silently and selects, among several on-screen options, the one that completes each item. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010, 2011, 2012 and 2013 cohorts it was administered in 6 sessions, from 7 to 10 years of age. The main outcome is the total score. Stability across successive administrations (median interval of 12 months) was ρ = .67. Stability across time points was ρ = .22–.63. Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .51–.66. ## Pending issues - Extreme value at 7.2 (form 1950): the maximum or minimum is more than 2 SD away from P99 or P1. Check in the raw data (possible timing or recording error). - The task has 2 forms; in 2 of 2 comparisons they have different scales. Norms are given by form (see "Forms"). - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
